title: A forgiven loan, a second emergency grant and rising City payments, all at once
question: Which City-funded organisations drew pandemic money from several public sources in the same months, where the same payroll or rent could have been charged twice?
finding: 9 City payees had a forgiven paycheck-protection loan of $100,000 or more and at least one other federal emergency source; for 7 of them City payments also rose 10% or more between fiscal 2019 and 2021. Those 7 had $19.3 million forgiven and $14.0 million from the other sources.
how: Loans are the SBA's records for borrowers whose name equals a City payee. The second source is any of: a Coronavirus Relief Fund award in the federal oversight file (through the City or the State of California), a Shuttered Venue Operators Grant, or an HHS Provider Relief Fund payment, matched by name, $100,000 or more. Relief-fund awards from other states and counties are left out because they pay for work done for those governments. City payments are by fiscal year from the City ledger.
limits: In 2020 it was the point of the programmes. What is not allowed is charging the same cost to two of them: a forgiven loan had to cover payroll that no other federal grant paid for. Nothing here shows that happened; it shows where an auditor would have to look, and no record on file shows that anyone did. Matches are by name.
